headline: Tishomingo County Schools Awarded Pre-K Grant with Program Planned for 2027, Board Considers Gate Fee Increase
summary: The board accepted a $300,000 State Invested Pre-K grant, with the program planned to begin in August 2027, and approved personnel, field trips, fundraisers, workers' compensation coverage and technology and professional development contracts. It heard a proposal to raise athletic gate fees, deferring a final vote, and authorized the superintendent to negotiate the purchase of property behind Burnsville School.

personnel.note: Hires: an ISD assistant teacher, a cafeteria worker and a custodian (one hire was an employee moving from a position the same meeting accepted a resignation from); other = 3 leave requests, 1 non-employee volunteer football coach and 1 certified athletic trainer approved for the 2026 football season.

money.item: State Invested Pre-K Cohort V Grant (partial), Aug. 20, 2026-June 30, 2029 (accepted)
Workers' compensation and employers liability, 10/1/26-10/1/27 (premium up $2,965 from last year)
money.vendor: Mississippi School Boards Association Workers' Compensation Trust

Quarterly HVAC filter service agreement, district-wide
GoGuardian technology filter, one year 10/1/26-9/30/27 (lowest quote)
Professional development for ATSI schools (lowest quote)
iCEV licenses, one-year subscription, sole source (CTE grant and district funds)
Tri-State Educational Foundation grant: Smart Board for IMS 7th/8th grade
Tri-State Educational Foundation grant: IMS 8th grade trip to Huntsville Space Center

superintendent: Superintendent Christie Holly discussed logistics for a pre-K program: classes limited to 20 students with one adult per 10 students, no district transportation for pre-K, and full operation required by August 2027.
Holly updated the board on the press box project.
The district received 2 Vector bullying reports and 3 Google reports.
Financial auditors were in-house the week of the meeting, and an MDE Gifted in-district visit was scheduled for Sept. 15.
Fall Special Olympics will be held at Pontotoc; fall break is Oct. 5-9.
executiveSession: appeal of a student discipline matter
otherActions: Approved advertising for a Pre-K Director/K-2 Curriculum Director; board agreed to schedule a working session on the pre-K program

Gate fee increase proposed by the Belmont High and TCHS athletic directors (football $10; volleyball, basketball, baseball and softball $8; archery and junior high $6; annual, student, veteran and senior passes); board expressed support but will discuss further before a final vote
Authorized Superintendent Holly to negotiate purchase of property behind Burnsville School
Approved clinics/pharmacies to offer on-site voluntary flu vaccinations for employees beginning October 2026
Board President Jessica Seaton updated the board on Strategic Plan goals
22 field trip requests approved (one TCHS band request lists four destinations; some retroactive)
Next regular meeting set for Oct. 12, 2026
